author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The Dashwood family had lived in Sussex for many years. They owned a large estate called Norland Park, and because they were wealthy and respectable, everyone in the neighborhood thought highly of them.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The old owner of the estate was an elderly bachelor. After his sister died, he was lonely, so he invited his nephew Henry Dashwood, along with Henry's wife and daughters, to live with him at Norland Park. They brought a lot of happiness to the old man in his final years.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: When the old man died, everyone was very disappointed by his will. He didn't leave the estate to Henry Dashwood so he could sell it or pass it to his daughters. Instead, he made a rule that the estate had to go to Henry's son from his first marriage, John Dashwood, and then to John's young son.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: The old man had grown very fond of Henry's young grandson, Harry, because the little boy was loud and energetic. Because of this, he left the entire estate to the boy, completely ignoring the years of care and attention he had received from Henry's daughters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Henry Dashwood was initially very upset by the will. However, he was an optimistic person, and he thought that since he was healthy, he could save up enough money from the estate's income to leave a good inheritance for his wife and daughters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Tragically, Henry Dashwood only lived for one year after inheriting the estate. Because he died so quickly, his widow and daughters were left with only a small inheritance of ten thousand pounds to live on.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Before he died, Henry Dashwood asked his son John to come see him. On his deathbed, Henry strongly urged John to help take care of his stepmother and half-sisters financially.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: John Dashwood wasn't a very emotional or deeply caring person, but he felt guilty because of the situation, so he promised his dying father that he would do everything he could to make them comfortable.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: John Dashwood wasn't necessarily evil, but he was very selfish and calculating. His bad traits were made worse because he married a woman who was even more narrow-minded and selfish than he was.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Right after his father died, John thought about giving his half-sisters a thousand pounds each to fulfill his promise. He felt this would be a very generous and generous thing to do, and it made him feel good about himself.
